requirements.text: The system shall manage customer accounts.
The system shall manage an online store inventory.
The system shall manage a customer’s “Shopping Cart”.
The system shall confirm orders.
The system shall have an unambiguous interface to assist in browsing the categories and products.
The system shall use Secure Socket Layer (SSL) for security.
The system shall have an availability of 99.999%.
The system shall allow an optional mirror site for reliability and backups.
The system shall feature an interface for future software enhancement via “Plug-ins”.
Customers will be able to create accounts to store their customer profiles, configure contact information, view their purchase history, and confirm orders.
Customers will be able to register, log in, and log out of their accounts.
The inventory management will allow for administrators to update the categories, the products placed in categories, and the specific product details.
Customers will be able to confirm the order after checkout.
The system will implement an Application Interface to allow for various plug-ins to interact with the system.
The WebOrder system shall send an e-mail confirmation to the customer that the items they ordered will be delivered to the shipping address along with tracking number.
The WebOrder system shall send an e-mail to System Administrator regarding any technical queries from customers or sales people.
The system shall comply with PCI-DSS Level 3 requirements for processing, storing, and transmitting credit card data, and implement a third-party fraud detection service for all transactions.
The system shall implement an account lockout policy after 5 consecutive failed login attempts for a duration of 15 minutes, and notify the user via email.
The system shall achieve 99.999% availability with an RTO of less than 5 minutes and an RPO of less than 1 minute for the mirror site failover.
The system shall perform automated incremental backups every 24 hours and full backups weekly, with a retention period of 30 days.
Plug-ins shall run in a sandboxed environment with restricted access to the core system API and database, and shall be validated via a digital signature check before execution.
The system shall retrieve 200 product records per second from the database under a load of 1000 concurrent users with a database size of 20,000 items.
The system shall implement asynchronous loading such that the Time to Interactive (TTI) for product pages is less than 2 seconds on a standard broadband connection.

OPEN: The PRD mentions storing credit card information in customer profiles but does not specify how this data is protected at rest or if it is stored at all. - The system shall not store full Primary Account Numbers (PAN) in the database; if storage is required, it must use industry-standard encryption (AES-256) and tokenization.

OPEN: The use of an 'open source firewall called Firestarter' is outdated and lacks context regarding configuration, maintenance, or rule sets. - The system shall be protected by a hardened firewall configuration (e.g., iptables/nftables) with a default-deny policy, specifically restricting access to only necessary ports (80, 443).

OPEN: The PRD mandates support for 1000 concurrent customers but does not define the expected transaction volume or data growth rate over time. - The system shall support 1000 concurrent users with a sustained throughput of 50 orders per minute and a database growth capacity of 20,000 items.

OPEN: The PRD specifies a requirement for 1000 concurrent users but does not define the expected transaction volume or peak load patterns (e.g., requests per second) to support this concurrency. - The system shall support a peak load of X transactions per second while maintaining the specified response time for 1000 concurrent users.

OPEN: The PRD lists an availability requirement of 99.999% in the scope but 99.99% in the quality attributes section. - Standardize the availability requirement to 99.99% (four nines) or 99.999% (five nines) consistently throughout the document.
